newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends softer on weaker bonds.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends softer on weaker bonds.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended slightly weaker on Thursday at C$1.3730 (US$0.7283) from this morning's open of C$1.3708 (US$0.7295) and much weaker than Wednesday's close of C$1.3677 (US$0.7311), under pressure from falling Canadian bonds. * Traders said the currency was also pressured by short-selling.
Traders said the Canadian dollar remained vulnerable to the wide spread between short-term Canadian and U.S. debt yields, which are currently about 250 basis points higher.
They said speculation that the Federal Reserve could hike U.S. interest rates after the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting July 1-2 would keep the Canadian dollar from strengthening too much.

The Bank of Canada resisted pressure to raise Canadian rates after the Fed raised U.S. rates by 25 basis points on March 25. Traders said another Fed raise would drive Canada's dollar sharply weaker if the Bank of Canada declined to follow.
Bank of Canada Deputy Governor Chuck Freedman indicated today the central bank had been trying to close the nation's gap between production capacity and current output by stimulating the economy.

"We have been trying to provide stimulus to the economy in order to close that gap," said Freedman. "We think those easier monetary conditions, lower interest rates in particular, are going to have a substantial effect on domestic demand."
Freedman said the central bank would like to duplicate the U.S. experience by closing the gap and keeping inflation low.

"We think 1997 is going to be a good year for (Canadian) growth, it will take up the slack," Freedman said. "We think 1998 will have considerable momentum as well and slack will be gradually taken up over that period."
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 84.51 yen from Wednesday's close of 83.59 and dipped to 1.2332 marks from Wednesday's 1.2376 marks.
